passages.title: Paid Time Off Policy
passages.text:
Requests for more than 3 PTO days need at least 14 calendar days' notice (two weeks) before the first day off. Requests of 3 PTO days or fewer have no minimum notice: submit them as early as practical. Count only the PTO days charged, not weekends or company holidays.
Notice is counted from the day you submit the request to the first day off. For example, a request submitted on a Monday for a full working week off starting two Mondays later meets the notice rule; the same request submitted the Friday before does not. A late request is not automatically declined, but your manager may decline it if the team can't cover your work.

passages.title: Paid Time Off Policy
passages.text:
You can cancel or change a request in the HR Portal. Approved PTO that you cancel before it starts is restored to your balance.
To extend approved PTO, submit a new request for the extra days; the notice and approval rules apply to the whole absence. If you need to come back early, tell your manager and change the request so the unused days are restored.

passages.title: Paid Time Off Policy
passages.text:
Your manager approves your PTO requests. A request for more than 10 consecutive PTO days must also be approved by your director. See the Approval Matrix (RSE-APR-01 §2).
Consecutive PTO days are counted as PTO days charged in one continuous absence; weekends and company holidays inside the absence don't count toward the total but don't break it either. Approvers consider project needs and team cover, and they should respond promptly so you can make plans.

passages.title: Paid Time Off Policy
passages.text:
Submit every PTO request in the HR Portal before the first day off. Tell your team and update your calendar once it is approved.
It helps to talk to your manager before submitting a longer request, especially around project deadlines or site milestones. Your request shows your dates, the PTO days charged and your remaining balance. Your manager is notified and approves or declines it in the HR Portal; you are notified of the decision. PTO is not approved until the HR Portal shows it as approved.

passages.title: Approval Matrix
passages.text:
Request | Approver
PTO up to 10 consecutive days | Manager
PTO over 10 consecutive days | Director
Field-role PTO in the December blackout | Director
Floating holiday | Manager
Sick time | None (notify your manager)
Parental, bereavement, jury duty | HR (manager notified)
Unpaid personal leave | HR
The rules behind these rows are in the Paid Time Off Policy (RSE-PTO-01), the Holiday Calendar & Observance policy (RSE-HOL-01) and the Leave of Absence Policy (RSE-LV-01). For example, a PTO request of 11 consecutive working days needs the director, while a request of 10 or fewer needs only the manager.

passages.title: Paid Time Off Policy
passages.text:
Field/site-based employees may not take PTO during the last two weeks of December, from December 18 to December 31, because of year-end site work. A field/site-based employee who needs PTO in that window must get a director's exception; the request goes to the director for approval.
Company holidays in the window, such as Christmas Day, are still company holidays. The blackout does not apply to office-hybrid or remote-approved employees, whose December PTO follows the normal rules. Field/site-based employees planning December time off should talk to their manager and director early in the autumn.

passages.title: Paid Time Off Policy
passages.text:
Interns earn 5 days of PTO per internship, whatever its length. Unused intern PTO is not carried over or paid out.
Interns request PTO in the HR Portal like everyone else, and the notice and approval rules in §4 apply. An intern who later joins Ridgeline as a full-time or part-time employee starts accruing under §2.1 or §2.2 from their new hire date.

passages.title: Approval Matrix
passages.text:
Request | Approver
Home-office stipend | Manager
Benefits changes | None (self-service in the window); HR for exceptions

passages.title: Paid Time Off Policy
passages.text:
If you leave Ridgeline, any payout of unused PTO is handled by HR at separation.
Plan your remaining PTO with your manager once you have given notice; approved PTO in your notice period is taken as normal. HR confirms your final balance and how it is handled in your final pay. Questions about your own situation go to the HR Service Desk.

passages.title: Approval Matrix
passages.text:
This matrix lists who approves each kind of request. "Manager" means your direct manager on the HR record. "Director" means your manager's director. "HR" means the HR Service Desk. "VP Finance" means the VP Finance, Tom Whitaker. Where a row says "none", no approval is needed, but you may still need to tell someone.
Approvals are given in the HR Portal unless a policy says otherwise. If your approver is away, their own manager can approve in their place. An approver cannot approve their own request; it goes to the next level up. The policies listed in each row hold the full rule, and this matrix only summarises who decides.

passages.text:
These are the observed US company holidays. Where the holiday's actual date falls on a weekend, the actual date is shown in brackets.

US offices are open on Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Presidents' Day and Columbus Day / Indigenous Peoples' Day; they are not US company holidays. Employees who want to mark them can use a floating holiday (§4).

passages.title: Holiday Calendar & Observance
passages.text:
On November 11 the Toronto office observes two minutes of silence at 11:00. Remembrance Day is a regular working day for the Toronto office, not a company holiday, so a Toronto employee taking PTO on November 11 is charged a PTO day for it. (For the US offices, November 11 is Veterans Day, a company holiday; see §2.)
Toronto colleagues working with US teams that week should expect the US offices to be closed on November 11, and US staff should not assume their Toronto colleagues are off. Staff of any office who wish to join the Toronto observance remotely are welcome to do so.

passages.title: Holiday Calendar & Observance
passages.text:
Full-time and part-time employees in the US offices get 2 floating holidays a year; employees in the Toronto office get 1 floating holiday a year. Interns do not get floating holidays. Request a floating holiday like PTO, in the HR Portal; it is not deducted from your PTO balance. Your manager approves it. Floating holidays do not carry over: unused floating holidays lapse at the end of the year.
Floating holidays let you mark days that matter to you, such as a religious or cultural holiday that isn't a company holiday, a birthday, or a day such as Martin Luther King Jr. Day for US staff. They are taken as whole days. New employees receive their floating holidays for the year they join, and they are not paid out when you leave.

passages.title: Holiday Calendar & Observance
passages.text:
When a holiday falls on a Saturday, it is observed on the Friday before. When it falls on a Sunday, it is observed on the Monday after. In Canada, when Christmas Day or Boxing Day falls on a weekend, each moves to the next working days. The tables below list the observed dates, which are the days the office is closed.
Only the observed date is a day off. If you are scheduled to work on the actual date because it falls on a weekend, for example on a project site, the substitute-day rule in §1.4 applies. The HR Portal shows each year's observed dates on your time-off calendar.

passages.title: Holiday Calendar & Observance
passages.text: A company holiday that falls inside your PTO dates is not deducted from your PTO. When you count the PTO days a request will use, leave out weekends and your home office's company holidays. For example, a Denver employee taking Wednesday to Friday off in a week where Wednesday is a US company holiday uses 2 PTO days, not 3. See also RSE-PTO-01 §3.2.

passages.title: Holiday Calendar & Observance
passages.text:
Part-time employees are paid for a company holiday if it falls on one of their scheduled working days. Field/site-based employees who are asked to work on a company holiday get a substitute day off within 30 calendar days, agreed with their manager.
A part-time employee whose scheduled days don't include the holiday is not given another day off in its place. Substitute days for field staff are recorded in the HR Portal and are not deducted from PTO; if the substitute day isn't taken within the window, talk to your manager and HR.

passages.title: Holiday Calendar & Observance
passages.section_heading: Your calendar follows your home office
passages.text: Your company holidays follow the calendar of your home office, the office on your HR record, not the place where you are working or travelling. Employees of the Denver, Austin and Seattle offices follow the US calendar (§2). Employees of the Toronto office follow the Canada calendar (§3). An Austin employee working in Toronto for a week still follows the US calendar, and a Toronto employee visiting Denver still follows the Canada calendar.
